subject: RE: NovaPay v2.0 - GDPR compliance sign-off
body:
Hi Sarah, Marcus,

I've completed my GDPR review of the NovaPay v2.0 payment token storage design.

My sign-off is conditional on the following being implemented before launch:
1. All payment token storage must be in eu-west-1 (AWS EU Ireland) only
2. Redis cache TTL for tokens must not exceed 24 hours
3. The NovaPay abstraction layer must include a data deletion method that our GDPR pipeline can call (for Article 17 requests)
4. No payment token may be logged in application logs — use a tokenized reference ID instead

If all four are met, I'll give final legal sign-off. Marcus, can you confirm in writing (this thread) once each point is implemented? I need the paper trail for our DPA audit in March.

Thanks,
James

subject: RE: NovaPay v2.0 - GDPR compliance sign-off
body:
James, Sarah,

Confirming all four items are implemented in GitHub PR #234:

1. ✅ EU region enforced in Terraform config, hard-coded to eu-west-1. No fallback.
2. ✅ Redis TTL set to 21,600 seconds (6 hours). Way under your limit.
3. ✅ Added `delete_token(user_id)` method to the PaymentProvider abstract class. Our GDPR pipeline can call it.
4. ✅ Application logs use payment_reference_id (a non-reversible hash). Actual tokens never appear in logs.

PR is open for your review. Tag you on GitHub too.

Marcus

subject: Quarterly architecture review - Django to FastAPI migration outcome
body:
Team,

As promised, here's the summary of the Django → FastAPI migration decision.

Why we moved:
- Django's ORM was causing N+1 queries in our payment processing pipeline that were hard to fix without rewriting large parts of the codebase
- FastAPI's async support (via asyncio) lets us handle concurrent webhook processing much better — we were dropping webhooks under load with Django's sync views
- Performance tests showed FastAPI handling 3.2x more requests/second for our payment endpoints

What we kept from Django:
- We're still using Alembic for migrations (not Django's migration system obviously, but same concept)
- The admin panel is staying as a separate Django app for internal tooling — the cost of migrating it wasn't worth it

Timeline: migration is complete for all core APIs as of July 2023. The admin Django app stays. Any new endpoints must be FastAPI.

If you're onboarding and see Django code — it's the admin panel, leave it alone unless you know what you're doing.

Marcus

subject: RE: Log retention policy - data team exception request
body:
Priya, Sarah,

Following yesterday's meeting, I'm documenting the agreed exception to the 90-day retention policy for the data/ML team:

**What's allowed:** Aggregated behavioral data with no user_id, no device fingerprint, and no IP address may be retained indefinitely for ML model training purposes.

**What's NOT allowed:** Any data that could re-identify an individual, even indirectly. This includes: small cohort sizes (< 100 users), sequential cohort IDs that could be correlated with signup dates, or any combination of attributes that narrows down to fewer than 100 users.

**Process:** Priya's team must submit the proposed anonymization schema to me for review before implementing any new data retention beyond 90 days. I'll respond within 3 business days.

This exception applies only to the data/ML team and requires annual re-confirmation.

James

P.S. This is now in the GDPR policy Confluence page (LEGAL-204).
